presentations.more: `boot` hands back work that is still in flight, and this statement throws the handle away. Nothing can wait for it, so the module's top-level code returns before the work is done and its callers are told it is; and nothing observes its failure, so a failure is lost without a trace — or, where the runtime treats an unobserved failure as fatal, ends the process. Wait for it, return it to the caller, or attach a failure handler; if dropping it really is intended, discard it explicitly where the language has a way to.

presentations.description: `Document.body` can return nothing in ordinary conditions, and its answer is used without a check, so the first member access throws.

derivedFacts: `Document.body` is documented to answer null or nothing
the answer's type does not state that it can be absent
nothing tests the answer before it is dereferenced

presentations.more: `Document.body` is documented to answer nothing in ordinary conditions — an unset variable, the end of a stream, a path that is not there — and the type this function sees does not say so, so the compiler lets it dereference the answer unchecked. When the answer is absent, the first member access throws. Test the answer, or supply a default, before using it.

specs.authoredModuleSummary: Documents runtime.mjs, the client and server runtime that hydrates islands, renders on the server, and bridges to Preact and React, exposing a rejectPath function that can throw an Error.
specs.description: `runtime.mjs` — Runtime. This project's call graph records DIRECT calls only, so a function passed to a container, destructured into an exported binding, or reached through a dynamic lookup is not one it can see. Within that limit it records no call to this module. At run time it reaches `core` and `panel`. Can fail: “`rejectPath` can fail with the error `Error`.” 2 requirements: 2 violated. 1 stated failure.
